title: Aerodynamics
tagline: Aerodynamic forces, potential flow, airfoil theory and panel methods, finite wings, viscous drag, shocks and expansions, and transonic and supersonic flow
summary: Aerodynamics explains how wings produce lift and what it costs in drag. The course builds from aerodynamic forces and potential flow to thin-airfoil theory, panel methods, finite wings and induced drag, and viscous effects and stall, and then turns to compressible aerodynamics: oblique shocks and expansion waves, subsonic and transonic airfoils, supersonic flow and the main features of hypersonic flight.

chapters.title: Aerodynamic forces and coefficients
chapters.summary: Lift, drag and pitching moment and their coefficients, the centre of pressure and the aerodynamic centre, and the similarity parameters of aerodynamics.

chapters.title: Incompressible potential flow
chapters.summary: Stream function and velocity potential, elementary flows and their superposition, flow over a cylinder and the Kutta–Joukowski theorem.

chapters.title: Airfoils and thin-airfoil theory
chapters.summary: Airfoil geometry and nomenclature, the Kutta condition, vortex sheets, and thin-airfoil theory for lift and pitching moment.

chapters.title: Panel methods
chapters.summary: Source and vortex panel methods for airfoils of arbitrary shape.

chapters.title: Finite wings
chapters.summary: Wing-tip vortices and downwash, Prandtl's lifting-line theory, induced drag, and the effects of aspect ratio and sweep.

chapters.title: Viscous effects, drag and stall
chapters.summary: Boundary layers on airfoils, skin-friction and form drag, transition, stall and high-lift devices.

chapters.title: Oblique shocks and expansion waves
chapters.summary: Oblique shock relations, the θ–β–M relation, Prandtl–Meyer expansions and shock-expansion theory.

chapters.title: Subsonic and transonic airfoils
chapters.summary: Compressibility corrections, the critical Mach number, drag divergence and supercritical airfoils.

chapters.title: Supersonic and hypersonic flow
chapters.summary: Linearised supersonic flow over thin airfoils, wave drag, swept wings, and the main features of hypersonic flow.
